**Reusable pieces and the needs they serve** *(positions of 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-25; filed from a condensed source)*.

The following is an analyst paraphrase of the curator's positions in the [Week 3 packet](../design/stage-15/week3/PACKET.md), Appendices A, B and C, not a verbatim quotation. His current picture is probably less a fixed pyramid than reusable series of actions with inputs, outputs and expected outcomes. An inherited drive or a dearly held learned structure can supply such a piece. Identifying which outcomes a piece serves matters more than assigning it one anatomical location. The inherited examples and the learned examples, including natalism, republicanism and honor, remain distinct sources of structure; their nesting does not make every structure a drive.

He proposes beginning with each system's need, the bad state it addresses, then reading its use under a stimulus and situation, including habits. Candidate motivations contribute according to how relevant they are to the observed action. A channel's transformations may constrain the kind of outcome being sought even without experimentally designed variation. Anger, including irritation, presupposes a stymied want on this account. FEAR and RAGE amplify or suppress other wants; they can operate automatically and partly without awareness. The proposed individual signal is a person's context-conditioned distribution of these uses, against the population, rather than an unqualified count of channel words.

PLAY is proposed to address broad uncertainty when the environment is safe, with FEAR blocking it. CARE is called the opposite of play in the supplied account: taking responsibility folds others into one's own decision tree, while discovering a good solution can produce a wish to share it, gain appreciation or respect, and learn from being copied that it works. These are the curator's proposed connections, not established functions of a single circuit. SEEKING must differ from RAGE; his tentative description is a scalar pointing toward a want. This supplements rather than establishes the earlier boredom conjecture.

LUST is retained as a distinct evolutionary system, perhaps deeper than the others. PANIC/GRIEF's name may mislead and its function is explicitly unresolved. Neither is to be absorbed into a simple copying account of the other channels. The proposed phylogenetic clue is provisional: only LUST and perhaps PANIC/GRIEF and CARE looked datable to him. The channels are held to be largely inherited and partly learned. Their triggers and confusing nuances are the object of explanation, not settled labels. The top of the chain may be persistence, with people as imperfect optimizers, but he explicitly finds that top hazy. Confidence: untested, logic only.

**Learned ends and the present goal distribution** *(2026-10-21 and 2026-10-25)*.

Analyst paraphrase of the curator's condensed positions in the [Week 3 packet](../design/stage-15/week3/PACKET.md), Appendices A, B and C: inherited solutions and dearly held learned structures can both be pieces serving external outcomes. Learned structures such as honor can become ends, as a person's guess at serving the top of the chain. Persistence is a tentative candidate for that top, not a settled universal goal. His target is the distribution of higher-order goals a person serves and its divergence from the population, conditioned on the stimulus, available actions and habits. A weighted set of relevant motives is one proposed reading of a decision. Calling a rate higher or lower than optimal additionally requires an independent account of success; population agreement alone supplies no optimum.

The wanting-to-want attentional channel remains central in his account. A second look may expose the higher goal being served, as when someone notices and corrects their own micro-racisms. What a person would sacrifice, including small local costs, is proposed evidence that something is an end. This keeps present endorsement, historical repetition and the outcome probes distinct: a recurring act alone does not settle which need or end it serves. Confidence: untested, logic only.

**Current trust, selective uptake and repetition** *(2026-10-25)*.

Analyst paraphrase of the curator's condensed morning and walk positions in the [Week 3 packet](../design/stage-15/week3/PACKET.md), Appendices A, B and C: the central target is the human ability to know someone well enough to decide whether to trust them and update one's own weights from them. Knowing a person's bad parts does not require engaging with those parts. Filtering can operate on part of the transition map by declining to model its reasons, using a quick dispositional label instead; attention is the proposed cost. The reader may take a useful move bundled with an unwanted end when the move can be repurposed and that end starved of support.

Trust refers to the current projected map and shared ends, not to a track record by definition. The curator notices that he tends to assume even the worst historical actors shared humanity's core goals and erred in means; he explicitly leaves that assumption in doubt. If ends are shared, kindness too could be a failure to optimize. His proposed explanation of betrayal is learning that the person would do it again, making aloneness the expected outcome, engaging grief or separation distress and sending one toward others. These are proposed mechanisms, not measurements of a person from a writing log.

Indoctrination is proposed to begin with the sense that a move might sometimes make sense, followed by repetition until it becomes a default autocomplete in flow. Absorption would appear in automatic behavior that was not receiving attention. His track-record concern is a tradeoff between confidence about a lifetime trajectory and confidence about what the person wants now; whether that is an anti-capture mechanism remains a question. The Heisenberg label is his analogy, not a claim of a quantum or mathematical impossibility. Confidence: untested, logic only.
